Baseline implementation: Normalizes work orders, train windows, configuration and work-order IDs; validates candidate inputs in solver_engine._normalise_inputs.
CP-SAT implementation: Uses baseline normalization helpers in cpsat_solver._normalise_inputs and the shared candidate-start generator.
Equivalence assessment: Shared behavior for normalized fields; common helper bugs are not independently detected by comparing the two solvers.
Promotion requirement: Validate normalized domain against the approved schema and an independent input validator.

Baseline implementation: Generates starts on the existing time grid, within its modeled horizon/duration rules; filters starts overlapping listed same-section/same-line train occupancy.
CP-SAT implementation: Uses the same baseline candidate-start generation/filtering behavior before creating optional intervals.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent for shared candidate construction on inputs representable by both; not proof that the grid/horizon matches operations.
Promotion requirement: Approve time resolution, horizon, date semantics, rounding and conservative clearance.

Baseline implementation: Rejects candidate when listed train window conflicts on same section and line; heavy work also filters adjacent-line train overlap.
CP-SAT implementation: Reuses baseline candidate filter and therefore inherits the same listed-train and adjacent-heavy rules.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent on listed intervals; neither proves timetable completeness or authenticates train inputs.
Promotion requirement: Use authenticated complete occupancy evidence and independently validate every returned assignment.

Baseline implementation: Compatibility is section/line keyed. Different lines are treated as compatible.
CP-SAT implementation: Uses section/line interval groups and shared compatibility rules.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent for current identifiers, but no real topology/possession graph is modeled.
Promotion requirement: Define and test validated section, line, adjacency and possession semantics.

Baseline implementation: Overlapping jobs in same section, line and department are incompatible.
CP-SAT implementation: Optional intervals are grouped by section/line/department and constrained with NoOverlap.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent for the modeled grouping and interval representation.
Promotion requirement: Add boundary tests for half-open intervals, same endpoints and precision conversion.

Baseline implementation: Different department work may overlap only when interval, section and line match exactly and both permit co-location.
CP-SAT implementation: Uses shared _compatible behavior and pairwise Boolean incompatibility for overlapping cross-department choices.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent in current helper semantics, subject to CP-SAT interval precision and Boolean encoding.
Promotion requirement: Independently test all co-location flag combinations, intervals and shared-resource interactions.

Baseline implementation: Different track lines are compatible; no heavy-equipment maintenance-vs-maintenance exclusion.
CP-SAT implementation: Reuses baseline compatibility; no cross-line maintenance conflict is added.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent but potentially incomplete operational rule; equivalence is not a safety endorsement.
Promotion requirement: Operations/safety owner must decide adjacent worksite conflict and define physical constraints.

Baseline implementation: No 1 km/2 km distance constraints in candidate generation or baseline solver.
CP-SAT implementation: No spatial buffer constraint in CP-SAT formulation.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent omission. Safety verifier applies separate geometric rules and generally lacks generated worksite endpoints.
Promotion requirement: Model approved worksite/equipment geometry or fail closed with validated evidence in independent verification.

Baseline implementation: No crew calendars, skill eligibility, or cumulative crew capacity.
CP-SAT implementation: No crew/skill variables or resource constraints.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent omission due to unavailable schema fields.
Promotion requirement: Add approved resource data and capacity/eligibility constraints before operational claims.

Baseline implementation: `heavy_equipment` changes train conflict handling; no equipment inventory/type/capacity constraint.
CP-SAT implementation: Same heavy-equipment flag usage; no equipment resource constraints.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent narrow boolean behavior, not equipment availability or capacity.
Promotion requirement: Define equipment inventory and task compatibility; add capacity and competition tests.

Baseline implementation: Fixed duration, one contiguous assignment interval; overlap uses half-open comparisons.
CP-SAT implementation: Fixed optional interval; integer start/end/duration variables and NoOverlap.
Equivalence assessment: Similar but not proven bit-for-bit equivalent for all accepted fractional durations due to CP-SAT precision/scaling.
Promotion requirement: Specify duration/time precision and prove exact conversion or document/approve rounding.

Baseline implementation: No per-order earliest/latest start, deadline, dependency, travel/setup, or rest fields/constraints.
CP-SAT implementation: No such fields/constraints in CP-SAT formulation.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent omission; shared absence is a domain gap.
Promotion requirement: Define authoritative inputs and constraints; test invalid sequences/windows.

Baseline implementation: Used to order variables/values and influence search heuristic; not a hard deadline or explicit weighted priority.
CP-SAT implementation: Used in decision ordering; coverage and secondary objective do not explicitly weight urgency.
Equivalence assessment: Not equivalent to an operational priority guarantee; heuristic ordering does not define objective preference.
Promotion requirement: Approve explicit priority semantics and verify objective/constraint ordering.

Baseline implementation: First searches for a complete solution. If complete search exhausts, greedy fallback can return a partial schedule; it does not prove that the partial contains maximum possible orders.
CP-SAT implementation: First maximizes scheduled order count, then optimizes secondary score at proven maximum coverage.
Equivalence assessment: Different semantics. A partial baseline fallback need not match CP-SAT's maximum-coverage subset or count.
Promotion requirement: Choose a canonical coverage objective and compare exact scheduled/unscheduled ID sets on controlled instances.

Baseline implementation: Disruption cost, department/shift workload balance and co-location reward; bounded A* and optional simulated annealing search behavior.
CP-SAT implementation: Coverage first, then integer-scaled disruption/workload/co-location score; no baseline simulated annealing.
Equivalence assessment: Related terms, but not proven equivalent: lexicographic priority, integer scaling, rounding, search method and SA differ.
Promotion requirement: Approve priorities and weights; independent objective calculator; exhaustive optimality comparisons where tractable.

Baseline implementation: Does not return a global objective-optimality certificate; A* is bounded and simulated annealing is heuristic.
CP-SAT implementation: Can report objective optimal only when CP-SAT returns the corresponding optimal status after the coverage phase.
Equivalence assessment: Not equivalent proof capability; CP-SAT proof is valuable but only for its encoded/scaled model.
Promotion requirement: Expose proof state separately from feasibility; validate exact objective correspondence first.

Baseline implementation: Backtracking distinguishes exhaustion from node-limit cutoff; cutoff does not establish infeasibility. Greedy fallback may still return a partial schedule.
CP-SAT implementation: CP-SAT maps feasible/optimal/infeasible/unknown termination; time limit can stop proof with an incumbent.
Equivalence assessment: Different algorithms and termination states; do not map cutoff to unschedulable or incumbent to optimal.
Promotion requirement: Regression-test all termination statuses and maintain proof/termination metadata end to end.

Baseline implementation: Can emit `status=partial` and `solver_outcome=unschedulable` when full assignment search is exhausted but fallback returns a partial schedule.
CP-SAT implementation: Can emit `status=partial` and `solver_outcome=partial` for a proven maximum-coverage incomplete assignment.
Equivalence assessment: Known difference. In two preserved constraint cases scheduled counts and status match but outcome labels differ; labels describe different solver semantics.
Promotion requirement: Define consistent API meanings for global complete infeasibility and maximum-coverage partial; do not conceal solver-specific proof.

Baseline implementation: Returns `no_work`, empty schedule and no unscheduled IDs.
CP-SAT implementation: Returns `no_work`, empty schedule and no unscheduled IDs.
Equivalence assessment: Equivalent solver semantics. It is not a safety verification result.
Promotion requirement: Keep API `no_work` distinct; empty schedule/audit must never become verified success.

Baseline implementation: Response computes scheduled IDs and unscheduled submitted IDs after line combination/fallback; contract includes unscheduled_work_ids.
CP-SAT implementation: Response preserves submitted IDs and computes unscheduled IDs from CP-SAT selected assignments.
Equivalence assessment: Intended invariant is equivalent; benchmark/task tests cover accounting, but production integration still needs output validation.
Promotion requirement: Assert a duplicate-free disjoint partition of submitted IDs for all paths including errors, fallback and combined lines.

Baseline implementation: Production main imports/calls baseline and independently invokes verifier; strips solver FOL/isolation claims and provides no timetable coverage.
CP-SAT implementation: Not called by production API; CP-SAT metadata is not evidence and has no current API trust path.
Equivalence assessment: Not comparable as production paths. CP-SAT has no demonstrated end-to-end API verification behavior.
Promotion requirement: Before integration, validate CP-SAT output independently and run the same fail-closed authenticated-evidence verifier.

Baseline implementation: Existing tests exercise solver, outcomes, and selected constraints; no exhaustive operational model validation.
CP-SAT implementation: Tests include three tiny exhaustive-reference cases and curated constraints; CP shares baseline helpers.
Equivalence assessment: Evidence is limited; three small cases do not establish equivalence over all domains, resources, precision, or operational constraints.
Promotion requirement: Expand independent reference/property tests across approved constraints and boundaries; document every unmodeled requirement.

Baseline implementation: 30 preserved runs at sizes 10/25/50; all returned full schedules; search-cap hits recorded; no global objective proof.
CP-SAT implementation: 120 paired runs at four time limits; all returned full schedules and proved maximum coverage; objective proofs vary by size/limit.
Equivalence assessment: Same digests across 120 pairs, but no paired objective comparison is interpretable because baseline optimality is never proven. Inputs share fixed timetable windows.
Promotion requirement: Use representative governed inputs, matched objective/constraints, proof-aware comparisons, more independent scenarios and uncertainty reporting.

Baseline implementation: Two partial cases show status=partial and outcome=unschedulable.
CP-SAT implementation: The same two cases show status=partial and outcome=partial.
Equivalence assessment: The preserved CSV labels both rows classification=equivalent although same_solver_outcome=False; Task 12 report prose explicitly says the different outcomes must not be read as equivalent.
Promotion requirement: Do not edit historic results for this assessment. Future output generation must derive classification consistently from outcome and status fields and test that invariant.
